raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Leave Grand Central behind and head for the Chrysler Building, about five minutes on foot.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Walter P. Chrysler paid for this tower out of his own pocket, and he gave his architect, William Van Alen, one instruction — build me something higher than the Eiffel Tower.","source_id":"26c97779-1469-4747-a0c4-9e051499b3b1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1,"also_cites":["d73620e8-c6ae-4200-9aba-e7fe9e24d805"]},{"text":"Trouble was, the men behind the Bank of America wanted the exact same crown, so they hired Van Alen's former partner and sworn enemy, H. Craig Severance, to put up the world's tallest building down on Wall Street.","source_id":"26c97779-1469-4747-a0c4-9e051499b3b1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Severance finished first, at 927 feet, and figured he'd won.","source_id":"26c97779-1469-4747-a0c4-9e051499b3b1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Then Van Alen sprang the surprise he'd been assembling in secret inside the building — a 185-foot spire of seven radiating steel arches, hoisted up through a false roof and bolted in place in about ninety minutes.","source_id":"bec7203f-48ed-48c1-9aae-0e9ee12b7157","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1,"also_cites":["26c97779-1469-4747-a0c4-9e051499b3b1"]},{"text":"That silver spike shot the Chrysler to 1,046 feet, a full 117 feet over Severance's tower — an unbeatable margin.","source_id":"26c97779-1469-4747-a0c4-9e051499b3b1","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Severance, who'd been certain his own Wall Street skyscraper would top the world, was outraged; the spire, people said, was as much an act of vengeance as of engineering.","source_id":"bec7203f-48ed-48c1-9aae-0e9ee12b7157","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"And yet the Chrysler wore the world's-tallest crown for barely a year before the Empire State Building snatched it away.","source_id":"d73620e8-c6ae-4200-9aba-e7fe9e24d805","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1,"also_cites":["866b21c5-7e8e-4c42-ab0b-4bcb2691537d"]},{"text":"Still, this is art deco at its peak — the useful fused with the beautiful, and one of the finest examples ever built.","source_id":"d73620e8-c6ae-4200-9aba-e7fe9e24d805","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1,"also_cites":["866b21c5-7e8e-4c42-ab0b-4bcb2691537d"]},{"text":"The style had taken its name only in 1925, at the Paris Exposition Internationale des Arts Décoratifs, and its sunbursts, chevrons, and zigzags soon turned up on everything from jewelry to comic books to trains, remaking New York into a silvery science-fiction metropolis.","source_id":"c2195a56-b95c-4589-8bc5-94da8c200a18","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"For the best view from the street, go to the corner of Lexington Avenue and 43rd Street and look straight up.","source_id":"fea48d2c-c710-442f-8b8f-e1071df884d6","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"That scalloped crown sits on the tower like a jaunty jester's cap.","source_id":"866b21c5-7e8e-4c42-ab0b-4bcb2691537d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"Steel American eagles crouch at the corners of the 61st floor, angular and gleaming, as if ready to leap.","source_id":"fea48d2c-c710-442f-8b8f-e1071df884d6","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1,"also_cites":["866b21c5-7e8e-4c42-ab0b-4bcb2691537d"]},{"text":"Lower down, on the 31st floor, winged hubcaps echo the radiator caps of a 1929 Chrysler — the carmaker's signature carved in steel.","source_id":"fea48d2c-c710-442f-8b8f-e1071df884d6","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1,"also_cites":["d73620e8-c6ae-4200-9aba-e7fe9e24d805","866b21c5-7e8e-4c42-ab0b-4bcb2691537d"]},{"text":"There's no restaurant or observation deck up top, but the lobby — once a Chrysler showroom — is a lavish consolation.","source_id":"c8848846-2ed6-48b5-91dd-fcd6c7d8f400","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1,"also_cites":["d73620e8-c6ae-4200-9aba-e7fe9e24d805"]},{"text":"Amber light warms dark African wood and marble set against the brash steel of industrial America.","source_id":"c8848846-2ed6-48b5-91dd-fcd6c7d8f400","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"The elevators are the real jewels, their Egyptian lotus patterns inlaid with Japanese ash, Oriental walnut, and Cuban plum-pudding wood.","source_id":"c8848846-2ed6-48b5-91dd-fcd6c7d8f400","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"And overhead spreads Edward Trumbull's ceiling mural, Transport and Human Endeavor — said to be the world's largest — full of airplanes, buildings, and workers on Chrysler's assembly lines.","source_id":"c8848846-2ed6-48b5-91dd-fcd6c7d8f400","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1},{"text":"For the whole building at once, though, you'd have to cross town and look back from the deck of the very tower that beat it — the Empire State Building.","source_id":"d73620e8-c6ae-4200-9aba-e7fe9e24d805","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":1}]}
